gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a Type C (Europlug) plug is rated to only 2.5 A at 250 V under EN 50075, about 575 W on 230 V mains, while US-to-Europe Type C adapters advertise '2500 W (250 V, 10 A)'. None states either that the '20 W' on TESSAN's Type C Europe adapters drops to 15 W shared across all three USB ports.
standout_why: Compared against these pages: packandporter.com (Europe picks), wpa-pool.com (12 picks), thefinerroute.com (5 universal picks) and universaltraveladapter.net/europe (TESSAN line-up). wpa-pool repeats the makers' AC ceilings as stated ('2500W at 250V and 10A' for TESSAN, One Beat and LENCENT Type C adapters; '2400W at 240V' for EPICKA). Its own summary admits the Europlug 2.5 A limit is 'not mentioned anywhere'. packandporter and thefinerroute give no AC rating at all. For TESSAN's Type C 2-pack, wpa-pool lists '1 USB-C at 3A (20W PD); 2 USB-A at 2.4A each' and leaves out the 15 W shared total. universaltraveladapter.net does say the GaN 65W's 65 W is on USB-C3 alone, so that part of the USB finding is already covered (partial overlap).
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's pick, a Type C adapter, for phones, cameras and laptops: a 65–100 W laptop brick is far below the plug's 575 W. It changes the advice for anyone bringing a dual-voltage hair tool. A Type C plug's rated limit is about 575 W, so the adapter's '2500 W' claim does not make it a hair-dryer adapter. For that, a grounded Type E/F (Schuko) adapter is the right buy in France and Germany. On USB, the TESSAN Type C adapter charges one phone at 20 W but only 15 W in total once three devices are plugged in. On the WTA07 and WTA09, only port C3 does 65 W, and every other port is capped at 15 W. So a traveller charging a laptop and a phone together needs the laptop on C3.

findings.label: Europlug (Type C) rated current and voltage
findings.value: 2.5 A at up to 250 V (575 W at 230 V)
findings.note: Source text: 'rated for voltages up to 250 V and currents up to 2.5 A', defined by CENELEC EN 50075 (CEE 7/16 Alternative II). Arithmetic: 2.5 A × 230 V = 575 W. Same page: designed to fit Type E, F and K sockets, 10 A Type L (Italy) except the 16 A CEI 23-50, and all SN 441011 (Swiss) socket types. This is a secondary source. The IEC world-plugs page returned 403. It is the standard's rating for the Europlug, not a rating measured on any adapter.

findings.product: TESSAN US to European Travel Plug Adapter Type C (TA02USEU)
findings.label: Advertised AC pass-through vs Europlug rating
findings.value: Advertised 2500 W (max 250 V, 10 A); Europlug standard rating 2.5 A (575 W at 230 V)
findings.source_title: TESSAN US to European Travel Plug Adapter Type C
findings.note: Maker text: 'turns 1 EU socket into 4 American AC outlets and 3 USB ports, max capacity up to 2500 watt (max 250 Volt, 10 A)'. 10 A × 250 V = 2500 W is the maker's number. The maker does not say its round-pin plug meets EN 50075. The footnote: a 10 A claim on a 2-pin Type C plug is four times the Europlug standard's 2.5 A. Price $25.99 on tessan.com, in stock.
